### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-email`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via EmailService (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `db7392c1729a4c297c9bda0f74c704fe83c23b3f` — the merge of head `8130a2947ec44122fa1c97ad304f3143f928311e` into base `f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin db7392c1729a4c297c9bda0f74c704fe83c23b3f && git checkout db7392c1729a4c297c9bda0f74c704fe83c23b3f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341 8130a2947ec44122fa1c97ad304f3143f928311e && git checkout -B drift-repro f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341 && git merge --no-ff 8130a2947ec44122fa1c97ad304f3143f928311e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f71bb413592bda8a1ce757969d8ae2ce8577f341` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cdec9c78b35fad90afb396a1cb4f3ee49395c17e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.test.ts, packages/rest/src/email-send-display-name.test.ts, .changeset/32108-email-send-typed-fields.md (declaration lines and ADR-0087 marker only) + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts (`SendEmailInput`), packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts (the door's catch), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts (`mail/test`, the `email.send.async` subscriber), packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts and template-renderer.ts

Narrowing face (PR body and changeset both open `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`), so the floor is the whole diff outside the prose faces. Inputs: card #32108 (body, comments 6763249773, 6765141847, 6767399451; no ruling on the thread), the PR body, its four-file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `e1146e8063`, +154 / -0), and the head's check-runs. Author login is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay note is owed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set of `normalizeMessage` (exported from the package entry), `IEmailService.send`, `sendInline`, and through them `POST /api/v1/email/send`: narrows. Right, and correctly declared.** Newly refused: a `subject`, `text` or `html` whose value is neither `undefined`, `null` nor a string. Read against `SendEmailInput` on this head (`subject: string`, `text?: string`, `html?: string`): every newly refused value is outside the declared type. That includes the shapes the tests do not name: a boolean (`subject: false` used to send the word, `text: false` beside a string `html` used to pass the truthiness check), a `Buffer` or stream body (nodemailer would have taken one; the contract never declared it), and a boxed `String`. No string value changes its answer: `assertTextField` returns on `typeof value === 'string'` and the lines after it are untouched.
2. **`null` / `undefined` stay absence on every path. Right.** `assertTextField` returns before judging either, and the presence checks below it are byte-identical to `main`. Paths read: `send` and `sendInline` both enter `sendInternal`, which calls `normalizeMessage` once; the REST door forwards the body to `send`; the legacy arm of the `email.send.async` subscriber calls `sendInline(data)`; `sendTemplate` calls `send`. The canonical queued arm (`deliverPersistedRow` over `rowToNormalized`) never reaches `normalizeMessage` and is unchanged.
3. **Refusal order moves for inputs that were already refused. Right, no accept-set effect.** The three type checks now run before `subject is required`, the body presence check and the recipient checks, so a body that is wrong twice (say `subject: 42` and `to: []`) names the text field first. Same status, same code, different reason text.
4. **REST door status and envelope: same as `to: []`. Right.** `email-routes.ts` is not in the diff; its catch maps any message opening `VALIDATION_FAILED` to `400` with `code: VALIDATION_FAILED` and the reason in `error`. The new throw carries that prefix, so it takes the identical branch the empty-recipient refusal takes.
5. **First-party producers of a non-string: none found. Right.** `sendTemplate` forwards `renderPlainTextTemplate` / `renderTemplate` / `htmlToText` output (each returns a string, the empty string for a falsy template); the messaging notification arm forwards `renderNotification` output, built with `String(...)` and `interpolate`; `mail/test` passes literals; plugin-auth sends only through `sendTemplate`. A numeric subject out of a template is not reachable: the renderers stringify.
6. **No type, export, schema key or stored shape moves. Right.** `kindOf`, `assertTextField` and `MessageTextField` are module-private; nothing under `packages/spec` is in the diff.
7. **The PR's universal sentence, "a present non-string `subject` is refused `VALIDATION_FAILED`, 400 at the door, and recorded as a rejection row", is WRONG for one JSON-reachable shape.** See ④ finding F1.

### ② Semver level

Matches what the diff publishes.

- `@objectstack/plugin-email: patch`: right. AGENTS.md step 3: a non-protocol change, breaking or not, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. `@objectstack/rest` carries a test-only hunk and publishes nothing new, so it needs no entry.
- `!` in the summary line and the `**BREAKING**` block: present, and the block states the migration (pass the three fields as strings).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right, line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset. A published accept set narrows and nothing widens.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Nothing a metadata author can write is refused: template rows and notification templates reach the send path only through renderers that return strings.
- ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right, exactly one marker. No key, export, option or stored shape is removed, renamed or re-shaped, so there is nothing for a migration to rewrite and no tombstone.
- Gate verdict: `Check Changeset` completed success on this head (read 2026-11-10T13:35Z).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags, from the report (6767399451) and the PR body:

- **File surface** (claim: `normalizeMessage` only, plus the door if that is where `to` is answered). Held. The only non-test source hunks are the three calls at the top of `normalizeMessage` and the two private helpers they call; `email-routes.ts` is untouched, which the read of the door confirms is correct. Putting the door pins in the existing real-plugin harness file is accepted.
- **Verification readings were taken on `fa2f882f`, not this head.** The head is a merge of `main` over it; the net diff against `main` is the same four files. The local readings are not this record's evidence; the head's check-runs are.
- **`pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally, repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `test:repo` left to CI.** Accepted as CI-owned. State on this head, read 2026-11-10T13:35Z: `Lint · ESLint` success; `Build Core`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Test Core (1/8 to 8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, two scoped lints and `Live E2E UI` still in progress. Completed success: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, filter. No failure at the time of reading; the unfinished runs are not vouched for here and remain the landing check's to read.
- **Ablation's first subject leg ran on a re-spelled subject read.** Settled in the tree: the shipped line is `String(input.subject ?? '').trim()`, identical to `main`.
- **Commit trailers, PR footer, additive refs in the shared `.git`.** Not contract matters; no judgment here.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `recordRejectedMessage` stores `String(raw.subject ?? '')`, so an object subject is logged as `[object Object]`. ESCALATED, not accepted as out of scope.** The finding understates the line. That same coercion is the reason this PR's own contract fails for one input (F1 below): it does not only record a misleading value, it can throw, and it runs on the refusal path this diff creates. It is fixed in this PR, on the claim's file, with the seat widening the surface from `normalizeMessage` to that one line of `recordRejectedMessage`. Region overlap with #31699 is the seat's to sequence.

### ④ Design judgment

Does the narrowing take a declared capability away, or make the spec's own refusal real? The second. `SendEmailInput` on `main` declares the three fields as strings; the diff refuses at run time what the type already excluded, at the single function every send path crosses, before the delivery row and the transport. Landing it in `normalizeMessage` rather than at the door is right: the door has no validator of its own for `to` either, and an in-process caller gets the same answer as an HTTP one.

`email-service.ts`, sentence by sentence: the `assertTextField` guard and `kindOf` agree with their jsdoc (an array is named before `typeof`, `null` never reaches `kindOf`); the `normalizeMessage` jsdoc line is accurate; the three calls precede every read of the fields. `email-service.test.ts` and the door test assert what the code does, including a falsy non-string (`text: 0`) beside a valid body, which is the case a truthiness-based check would miss.

Attempts to break it:

- **F1, must-fix. `subject: {"toString": 1}` answers 500, not 400, on this head.** Path, read in the tree: the door forwards the body; `assertTextField` throws `VALIDATION_FAILED` (it uses `typeof` only, correct); `sendInternal`'s catch calls `recordRejectedMessage`; that builds the row literal with `String(raw.subject ?? '')` BEFORE its own `try`, which wraps only `persistence.insert`. For an object whose own `toString` is not callable, `String()` throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` (OrdinaryToPrimitive: `toString` skipped, inherited `valueOf` returns the object). The TypeError leaves `recordRejectedMessage`, replaces the caller's `VALIDATION_FAILED`, fails the door's prefix test and is rethrown to the outer catch: `500 EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`. An array holding such an object does the same through `join`. Any JSON client can write it. In process, `send()` rejects with a TypeError and writes no rejection row. Three published sentences are false for it: the changeset's "refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the field ... Through the REST door that is `400`", its "still recorded as a `failed` rejection row", and the `assertTextField` jsdoc's "the same REST `400`". `main` answers 500 for this input too (the throw was inside `normalizeMessage` there), so it is not a regression; it is the remaining member of the class the card exists to close, a caller's malformed field reported as a server fault, and the same defect #29891 fixed for display names in `rawAddressText`. Fix: record the subject only when it is a string (the `text` / `html` columns beside it already do, `typeof raw.text === 'string'`), else `UNSTATED_COLUMN`; pin `subject: {toString: 1}` at the door (400, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, one rejection row) and in the service test. That fix also closes the dev's `[object Object]` finding.
- **F2, nit. Legacy `email.send.async` arm.** A raw pre-#5160 payload with a numeric subject used to deliver; it now throws on every redelivery, so the queue spends its attempt budget and each attempt writes a rejection row before the job dead-letters. The treatment is the one every other `VALIDATION_FAILED` already gets on that arm (the subscriber is outside the diff), and such a payload is outside the declared type, so the contract holds. A follow-up card for "a validation refusal is not retryable on the legacy arm" is the right home; naming the arm in the changeset's BREAKING block is the dispatching seat's prose-face call.
- **F3, nit. `null` is pinned as absence but still forwarded.** `normalizeMessage` copies `text` / `html` when `!== undefined`, so a `null` reaches `NormalizedEmailMessage` and the row as `null`, as on `main`. Unchanged behaviour, outside the diff's lines; noted because the diff now pins `null` as legal.
- **F4, nit. jsdoc wording.** `assertTextField` says "before any row or transport call"; a rejection row is written. The changeset's "before any `sys_email` delivery row" is the accurate spelling. `recordRejectedMessage`'s jsdoc list of what it records does not name the new refusal; it can be corrected with F1.
- No mismatch found with the `to: []` refusal: same throw prefix, same catch, same 400 envelope, same single rejection row. No first-party caller passes a non-string (① item 5).

F1 is a must-fix: FAIL. Its fix earns a delta review by this reviewer on the new head. F2 to F4 are nits and do not hold the round.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32108-email-send-typed-fields`
Reviewed-by: `session_012dn2Ae4fomvXPZ2AioCpY4`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8eb5676464b8675f9064308a401757c3ce43687f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.test.ts, packages/rest/src/email-send-display-name.test.ts, .changeset/32108-email-send-typed-fields.md (declaration lines and ADR-0087 marker only; unchanged in the delta) + read, not reviewed: packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts (the door's catch), packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts

**Delta record.** It reviews the one commit `cdec9c78..8eb56764` (three files, +51 / -4) against finding F1 of the round-0 record 6768781992, which reviewed `cdec9c78b35fad90afb396a1cb4f3ee49395c17e` in full and FAILED on F1 alone. Everything that record passed is carried forward where the delta does not touch it; the two records together are the full review of this head. Inputs: the delta diff, the tree at this head, the dev's round-1 report (6774515672 on #32108), and this head's check-runs. The new head has `cdec9c78` as its only parent; no merge of `main` rides in the delta.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **F1 is closed. Right.** `recordRejectedMessage` now builds the row's `subject` as `typeof raw.subject === 'string' ? raw.subject.trim() : ''`, falling to `UNSTATED_COLUMN`. Nothing coerces a non-string subject any more, so nothing can throw there. Traced on this head for `subject: {toString: 1}` and `subject: [{toString: 1}]`: `assertTextField` judges by `typeof` and `Array.isArray` only and throws `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming `subject` ("an object" / "an array"); `sendInternal`'s catch calls `recordRejectedMessage`, whose row literal now completes (the other columns read the value through `rawAddressText` or a `typeof` guard, and `reason` is the error's own string); one row is inserted at `status: failed`, `attempt_count: 0`, `subject: (none)`; the original error is rethrown; the door's catch sees the prefix and answers `400` with `code: VALIDATION_FAILED`. In process, `send()` rejects with the `VALIDATION_FAILED` error and the row is written.
2. **The rejection row's `subject` column changes for every non-string subject. Right.** A number used to be logged as its digits and an object as `[object Object]`; both are now `(none)`, and the row's `error` column names the field and the kind. That is the treatment `body_text` / `body_html` already had, and it closes the dev's round-0 out-of-scope finding. A string subject on any other refusal (no recipient, bad `from`) is recorded exactly as before, trimmed; `null` / absent is `(none)` as before.
3. **No accept-set or public-surface change beyond round 0. Right.** The delta touches a private method's row construction, two jsdoc blocks and tests. The three changeset sentences F1 made false (400 at the door, the `failed` rejection row, the jsdoc's "same REST 400") are now true for the shapes F1 named.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right. The changeset file is not in the delta: `@objectstack/plugin-email: patch`, `!`, the BREAKING block, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` stand as judged in 6768781992. The delta publishes nothing that needs a new line: a rejection-log column value for input that was never deliverable. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Surface.** The claim's surface was widened by the seat to `recordRejectedMessage`'s subject column; the delta stays inside it (that line, its comment, the method's jsdoc list, the `assertTextField` jsdoc, and the two test files).
- **PR body corrections owed, flagged by the dev.** The Acceptance note that calls the `[object Object]` row "reported to the seat, not fixed here" is now false, and the Verification section's readings name `fa2f882f`. Both are prose-face edits for the seat; neither is judged here.
- **`pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally** (as in round 0). CI answers it: see the check-runs below.
- **Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-10T17:36Z: all completed, no failure, none in progress.** Success: Auto Label, Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped (query-options erasure, slot lookup & corpus, tooling self-tests), Live E2E UI, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core and its shards 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI, Type Check (consumer gates, debt ledger, source gates, workspace), TypeScript Type Check, filter. The remaining sixteen runs are `skipped` (opt-in, queue, schedule and UI matrix jobs), the same set skipped on the round-0 head.
- No out-of-scope finding is open: the round-1 report carries none, and the round-0 one is fixed by this commit.

### ④ Design judgment

`email-service.ts`: the fix is the one F1 prescribed and the code agrees with its own comment sentence by sentence (`String()` either invents `[object Object]` or throws; only a string is recorded, as for the body columns). I looked for a second coercion on the refusal path and found none: `kindOf` never stringifies the value, the error message is built from the field name and the kind, and the door strips the prefix from a string it already holds.

**F4 (nit, round 0): fixed.** The `assertTextField` jsdoc now reads "before any `sys_email` delivery row or transport call" and names the `failed` rejection row, which is what happens. `recordRejectedMessage`'s jsdoc list now includes "a non-string `subject` / `text` / `html`".

Tests: the service pins assert the rejection, no transport call, and one row with `subject: '(none)'` for both shapes; the door pins assert 400, the code, the named field and one `failed` row for both. They pin what F1 asked for. The door pins do not assert the row's `subject` value; the service pins do, so nothing is unpinned.

Regression check against what round 0 passed: `normalizeMessage`, `assertTextField`'s body and `kindOf` are byte-identical to `cdec9c78`; `null` / `undefined` remain absence on `send`, `sendInline`, the door, the legacy `email.send.async` arm and `sendTemplate`; the `to: []` refusal takes the same catch and envelope. Nothing regresses.

Carried, unchanged, from 6768781992 and not holding this round: F2 (nit: a validation refusal burns the retry budget on the legacy queue arm; follow-up card) and F3 (nit: a `null` body is still forwarded as `null`). No new finding.

Reviewed-by: `session_012dn2Ae4fomvXPZ2AioCpY4`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8130a2947ec44122fa1c97ad304f3143f928311e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.test.ts, packages/rest/src/email-send-display-name.test.ts, .changeset/32108-email-send-typed-fields.md (declaration lines and ADR-0087 marker only) + read, not reviewed: packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/index.ts

**Delta record.** This head is a merge commit: first parent `8eb5676464b8675f9064308a401757c3ce43687f`, the head record 6774561589 passed (itself a delta on the full review 6768781992), second parent `main` at `f71bb41359`. It carries no change by the PR's author. The question is only whether the merge moved what those two records judged. It did not; the three records together are the full review of this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The PR's net diff is unchanged. Right.** Against its merge base at each head (`e1146e8063` for `8eb56764`, `f71bb41359` for this head), the diff over the four PR files has the same stable patch-id, `7279d0cf80fa`, and all four blobs are identical at both heads (`email-service.ts` `2d6b5d7ceef3`, `email-service.test.ts` `1cd64457a6e8`, the door test `54401784d577`, the changeset `947769de07a9`). The whole net diff against `main` at this head is still those four files, +203 / -2.
2. **`main` brought nothing into the judged code. Right.** `main` did not touch `email-service.ts` (so `normalizeMessage`, `assertTextField`, `kindOf` and `recordRejectedMessage` are byte-identical), `packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts` (the door's `VALIDATION_FAILED` catch), `packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts` (`SendEmailInput`), `template-engine.ts`, or the messaging `email-channel.ts` / `template-renderer.ts`.
3. **What `main` did change nearby is orthogonal. Right.** In `plugin-email` it adds an SMTP connect policy (`smtpConnect`, `SmtpConnectPolicy`): `email-plugin.ts` now builds its transports through two private helpers, `index.ts` exports three new types, and `transports/smtp.ts` grows. The `mail/test` `sendInline` call and the `email.send.async` subscriber, the two callers the earlier records read in that file, are not in those hunks. No accept set or refusal path on the send input moves.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right, as judged in 6768781992 and carried in 6774561589: the changeset blob is identical.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No dev flag is new on this head; the merge is the seat's.
- The PR body corrections named in 6774561589 (the `[object Object]` acceptance note, the head the Verification readings cite) remain the seat's prose-face edits.
- **Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-10T17:40Z: no failure; most still running.** Completed success: Auto Label, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Test UI, filter. In progress: Build Core, Check Changeset, every Lint job, Plan Test Core shards (the Test Core shards had not started), Live E2E UI, and the four Type Check jobs. Their conclusions are not vouched for here and remain the landing check's to read. On the previous head `8eb56764` every non-skipped run was green.
